subject: AcmeCloud requested data-use & subprocessor restriction — product/security sign-off needed
messages:
From: sarah.kim@acmecloud.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com, legal.ops@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-10-17T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: DPA redlines: data use clause + subprocessors

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement attached an initial redline to the DPA and flagged two items that are blockers for Acme to sign: 1) a clause that disallows any use of customer data for model training/derivative models, and 2) a request to restrict subprocessors to a short whitelist and require advance notice + approval for any new subprocessors.

I attached the redlined PDF (Acme_DPA_redline_v1.pdf). Can your team confirm whether Redwood can accept the training prohibition and the subprocessor approval language, or whether we need to propose a mitigated exception? We have internal timelines (contract must be signed by 10/31) so would appreciate a quick read.

—Sarah
Procurement, AcmeCloud
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: dev.patel@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-17T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA redlines: data use clause + subprocessors

Team — forwarding Acme's redline. Key asks: absolute ban on any use of customer data for training, and a subprocessor approval flow (Acme wants whitelist + approval). Attachments: Acme_DPA_redline_v1.pdf; I've also exported our current subprocessor list (Acme_DataMap_export_20261017.csv).

Questions for product/security:
- Is a strict no-training clause legally/operationally feasible for hosted Dedicated/Private customers? Any runtime or cost implications for offering that as an option?
- For subprocessors: can we commit to a 30-day notice plus an explicit approval step for named critical subprocessors? Or do we need to offer an exception path with limited carve-outs?

I think we should treat this as a potential contract exception tied to the deal (deal id ACME-2026-REDWOOD-42). Acme is pushing a 10/31 signature.

Thanks — Jonas
From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-17T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines: data use clause + subprocessors

Jonas / Dev — quick security read:

1) No-training clause: We can operationally support a contractual commitment to not use Acme customer data to improve models only if they are on Redwood Dedicated or a fully private deployment with customer-managed keys and clearly segmented storage. For Hosted multi-tenant customers, it's much harder to provide cryptographic assurance; we can offer a contractual promise but it carries higher risk and will need monitoring + periodic attestations.

2) Subprocessors: We maintain a dynamic subprocessor list (SaaS infra, analytics, telemetry, cloud providers for regional failover, etc.). Acme's ask for a whitelist + approval is feasible for a subset of critical subprocessors (e.g., telemetry vendor, analytics engine). However, requiring approval for every new subprocessor is not operationally scalable — we should propose: 30-day notice + right to object for critical categories within that window; for low-risk infra providers we can commit to notification only.

Security asks: if we agree to the no-training promise, Acme must be on Dedicated or Private AND we need to add auditability (monthly reports + SOC2 export) and a short carve-out for emergency security patching that doesn't use customer content for model training.

I'll draft suggested language to propose as a counter.
—Hannah
From: dev.patel@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-17T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines: data use clause + subprocessors

Thanks — product implications:

- No-training promise: If we require Dedicated/Private for this guarantee, we need to confirm capacity availability and lead time. Acme expects production throughput we can meet, but Dedicated pools may require a 4–8 week provisioning window depending on GPU type. There's also roadmap work: adding an explicit tenant isolation + data-silo flag for billing/analytics so we can produce the audit artifact Hannah mentioned — estimate 2 sprints to ship a minimal reporting view and an additional sprint for automated attestations. This could push acceptance beyond 10/31 unless we take a contractual interim approach.

- Subprocessor approval flow: Product supports a two-tier approach (critical vendors = approval within 30 days; non-critical = notification). We should include a clear definition for critical (data processors, telemetry, key management, audit log providers). Also need to avoid manual approvals at scale — propose automated approval for previously vetted vendors and an SLA for decisioning (5 business days) for new ones flagged as critical.

Recommendation: propose a counter-offer to Acme that: 1) Allows a no-training commitment only on Dedicated/Private with a required provisioning lead time; 2) Offers a 30-day notice + objection right for critical subprocessors and notification-only for others; 3) Includes an interim attestation schedule so Acme can sign by 10/31 while we finalize implementation (we provide a first attestation within 30 days of go-live).

If you want, I can draft the counter language for Legal to package.
—Dev
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: sarah.kim@acmecloud.com
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com, legal.ops@acmecloud.com, dev.patel@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines: data use clause + subprocessors — proposed path forward

Sarah — thanks for sending the redline. Internal read complete; summary and proposed path forward below.

Summary of constraints:
- Redwood can accept a contractual prohibition on using Acme customer data for model training only if the environment is Dedicated or Private (customer-managed keys recommended). For Hosted customers we cannot provide a cryptographic guarantee today.
- For subprocessors we propose a two-tiered approach: 30-day notice + right to object for critical subprocessors; notification-only for low-risk infra vendors.

Proposed counter-offer (can be incorporated as tracked changes):
1) Data use: Redwood agrees not to use Acme-provided customer content to train or improve models for other customers when Acme is deployed on Redwood Dedicated or Privately hosted instances with tenant isolation and KMS controls. For Hosted accounts, Redwood will not intentionally use Acme customer content for model training; however, Redwood cannot provide a cryptographic or absolute technical guarantee on multi-tenant Hosted deployments.
2) Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a current list of subprocessors and will give 30 days notice for any additions classified as 'critical' (data processing, telemetry, KMS, analytics). Acme will have a 30-day window to object; if unresolved, Redwood will engage a remediation plan or offer alternative hosting (Dedicated/Private) where applicable. Low-risk infra additions will receive notification only.

Operational asks from Acme if we agree: Dedicated provisioning lead time (4–8 weeks), monthly attestation reports for data handling (first attestation within 30 days of go-live), and a joint implementation plan for KMS and key handling.

Next steps:
- If Acme is comfortable with the above, we'll draft the counter language and have Legal (cc'd) package it into the DPA redline by EOD 10/20.
- If Acme insists on an absolute no-training guarantee for Hosted, we will need to escalate pricing and a custom compliance package (likely signed as an enterprise Private deployment).

Sarah, can you confirm which hosting option Acme prefers (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)? If Dedicated/Private, we'll prioritize provisioning and aim to deliver a counter DPA and initial attestation schedule by 10/20.

Thanks — Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
